findings.current: “I guess he finds me pretty annoying.”
findings.defect: The draft makes Jin the person Jeok finds annoying. Jin is saying Jeok must have been bothered by Gong, whom he immediately advises to keep his distance.
findings.rationale: The following lines explain that Jeok dislikes repeated conversation from people he is not close to and warn Gong to stay away.
findings.replacement: “You must have bothered him quite a bit.”

findings.current: I’m just a guest traveling with you now. Someone else is in the presiding chair.
findings.defect: “With you” makes Jeok sound like a guest of Gong’s party, rather than someone who chose to accompany Jin’s group.
findings.rationale: Jeok sends Gong to ask another person, and Gong then approaches Jin.
findings.replacement: I just tagged along as a guest. Someone else is in the presiding chair.
findings.source: 지금의 나는 단순히 동행을 자처한 빈객일 뿐이지, 좌장(座長)은 따로 있어.

findings.current: And Gong Iljung—the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord and Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect—shared the same concern.
findings.defect: The draft omits Jin’s false start on Gong’s name, losing the setup for the later Gong Piljung/Gong Iljung exchange.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly interrupts 공필 with 아니, 공일중; the mistaken name recurs in the scene’s joke.
findings.replacement: And the Zhongnan Sect Leader, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord Gong Pil—no, Gong Iljung—shared that concern.
findings.source: 그리고 종남파의 장문인인 풍운검군 공필. 아니, 공일중 역시 이와 같은 우려를 품고 있었다.

findings.current: But most of them probably didn’t notice how those stiff necks—so unused to bowing to anyone for so long—hid their faintly quivering lips.
findings.defect: The draft turns the elders’ stiff bows into “stiff necks” and their moving lips into trembling lips, obscuring how the bows conceal their private reply.
findings.rationale: The source says their bowing motions conceal subtly moving lips, immediately before their Sound Transmissions are revealed.
findings.replacement: But most of them probably didn’t notice that the elders’ stiff, unpracticed bows hid the slight movement of their lips.
findings.source: 오랫동안 다른 이에게 굽히지 않았던 탓에 뻣뻣하기 그지없는 그 고갯짓이, 미세하게 달싹이는 입술을 감추었음을.

findings.defect: “Clop” suggests a hoofbeat, but the sound accompanies Jin getting off his horse and stepping onto the ground.
findings.rationale: 저벅 denotes a footstep; the next sentence describes Jin dismounting and Ju Hwaran setting her feet on the ground.

summary: Several localized changes alter who is being discussed, how the elders conceal their private reply, and the setup to the name joke.
